AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Tomsguide ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: New Nvidia bug is killing SSDs — is it “AI code incompetence,” users ask?

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (608 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomsguide

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you haven't updated your Nvidia drivers recently, you may want to hold off.
  • The bug was found in the two most recent Nvidia GPU driver updates — specifically 621.14 and 621.24 — for the Nvidia GeForce Game Ready Driver.
  • The bug was discovered by TroubleGrid who reported that the bug causes the NVDisplay.Container.exe to write (save data) far too much information to an Nvidia log file that can degrade the SSD.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you haven't updated your Nvidia drivers recently, you may want to hold off. A newly discovered bug apparently can damage your PC by writing excessive amounts of data to solid-state drives (SSDs).

The bug was found in the two most recent Nvidia GPU driver updates — specifically 621.14 and 621.24 — for the Nvidia GeForce Game Ready Driver. The 621.24 revision was released on November 12.

The bug was discovered by TroubleGrid who reported that the bug causes the NVDisplay.Container.exe to write (save data) far too much information to an Nvidia log file that can degrade the SSD. It can result in as much as 30GB per hour.

Sources indicate that the executable already wrote log files before the updates but not that much. SSDs typically take years to degrade, but the excessive data written by this bug can speed up the process causing stuttering and mouse lag.

It has been revealed that on Reddit, I've seen a few posts about the bug with users complaining that this is why you never upgrade. "By principle I never ever update my drivers unless there are feature inclusions for let's say a newly introduced game I bought," one Redditor said.

Plenty of others agreed with that sentiment, and I'm inclined to say they're correct here.

The other half of the comments split between blaming AI-written code. Before his ouster, CEO Jensen Huang was pushing for Nvidia engineers to use more AI-generated code via chatbots and agents.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Or they were of the belief that Nvidia is purposely killing drives to force customers to pay more for newly introduced ones. Several called out Sam Altman and his recent claim that laptop RAM is a "terrible" allocation of a scarce resource.

"I honestly would not be surprised if they are doing this on purpose to kill our NVMe's," wrote a poster.

If we were to put blame on something, at this point, I'd say its AI-fueled incompetence, not AI-fueled greed, though that has led to said stupidity.

The easiest fix is to rollback your graphics card driver to version 621.01, which is the last known patch to lack this bug.

TroubleGrid listed a manual fix that requires you to set the Nvidia Display Container LS service to manual. Though it'll cost you. Basically, this can disable the Nvidia Control Panel and Nvidia App, meaning G-Sync color settings, display scaling, resolution overrides and more will not rock. "Do not disable the service outright if you use G-SYNC or a custom colour profile," the report warns.

If you need a temporary fix, you can stop the service, delete the log file and start again. However, the file will return and continue to grow in size.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We already knew there'd be a frantic clamour for GTA 6 this week, and we also knew plenty of players would be eyeing up Xbox's 'New Zealand trick' to get in on the action early. But it's now being reported that a whopping 2m UK and US players took advantage of the trick - which, for context, equals more than a third of New Zealand's actual population.

Industry observers note that here's a quick bit of background: Rockstar's regional release schedule meant GTA 6 debuted at midnight on 19th November everywhere, local time. As such, New Zealand was the first country in the world to see the hugely anticipated game go live, thanks to timezones. And because Xbox players can make purchases on any regional store easily, simply by changing their console's country, understandably impatient sorts opted to become temporary virtual New Zealand residents in their droves (on PlayStation, the process requires a regional account and payment in local currency so is more finicky).

In a recent development, in fact, according to data analytics firm Ampere Analysis, the early demand was such that 1.5m Xbox users in the US and 600,000 UK Xbox players briefly went Kiwi for the occasion of GTA 6's launch. Other countries highlighted by Ampere include Canada, where 200,000 Xbox players took the Upcoming Zealand plunge, Brazil (200,000 players), and Mexico (100,000 players).

By contrast, just 100,000 PlayStation players in the US opted to dive in early, reflecting, as Ampere notes, "the ease of being able to switch country in the account settings on Xbox consoles." And here's all that info in graph form:.

In a recent development, amusingly, Newly introduced Zealand's tourist board tipped a wink to the sudden influx of virtual 'visitors', telling them "We'd love to have you". It also cheekily offered a video of cheerful tourists admiring the country's resplendent natural beauty "Life," read the accompanying caption, "because we're getting GTA 6 first.".

Sources indicate that some hours later and the rest of the world can now finally, officially join in the GTA 6 fun, and it's a game worth playing. Eurogamer's Chris Tapsell called it an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in his five star GTA 6 review. And if you need some help getting through the game now it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough as well as a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Some very rough napkin math led to estimates that Take-Two Interactive expected to make as much as $3.5 billion during the Grand Theft Auto 6 launch period. It actually made more than that on the GTA 6 launch day: Rockstar notes the game pulled in $3.79 billion in "day one retail sales," making it "the biggest entertainment launch in history.".

Industry observers note that by way of comparison, Avengers: Endgame, ranked on Wikipedia as the highest grossing movie of all time, earned a little more than $2.9 billion over its entire theatrical run. GTA 6 crushed that by nearly $1 billion in a day.

"It is with immense gratitude that we enter a new chapter of Rockstar Games with the release of Grand Theft Auto 6," Rockstar Games president and co-founder Sam Houser noted. "We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world and we couldn’t be more excited to share this moment with you.".

Sources indicate that strauss Zelnick, CEO of publisher Take-Two Interactive, had previously said that preorder levels of Grand Theft Auto 6 were "unprecedented" but declined to reveal specifics. It turns out he wasn't kidding: Take-Two Interactive also revealed today that GTA 6 sold 32.5 million copies in pre-release, which it said is "a newly introduced record across all platforms.".

Those numbers are absolutely staggering: There was never any question that GTA 6 was going to be huge, but those launch days sales—sales from one single day—surpass Take Two's net revenue guidance for the entire quarter by nearly $400 million at the high end.

Recent findings suggest that given that there's still well over a month remaining in the holiday season, I'd expect that figure to rise significantly: I'm not an industry analyst but more than $4 billion before the year is over suddenly seems just about conservative. Beyond that, I won't even hazard a guess, but consider this: Grand Theft Auto 5, which sold a little over 11 million copies on its launch day in 2013, has now surpassed 230 million copies sold in total. The sky, to paraphrase one of Tom Petty's other songs, really is the limit.

Latest Update: A Survivor Legend Went Off About The Coin Flip, And Honestly She’s Right

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that A lot of Survivor fans are still in their feels about the coin flip, and let the record show, fan favorite and multi-time player Kelley Wentworth is among the frustrated.
  • Sources indicate that during her extended rant, Wentworth ran down a laundry list of complications.
  • We should have left that in season 50 along with Mr.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that A lot of Survivor fans are still in their feels about the coin flip, and let the record show, fan favorite and multi-time player Kelley Wentworth is among the frustrated. She dropped a video yesterday going off about the game mechanic and talking through in very specific detail exactly why she wants it gone.

Sources indicate that during her extended rant, Wentworth ran down a laundry list of complications. She brought up how Lewis apparently won the coin toss but then was told it didn’t count because it landed outside the little circular mat host Jeff Probst had put down. She brought up how every single fan with any time awareness knew he was going to lose the coin flip because there wasn’t enough time left in the episode to vote. And more broadly, she brought up the fact that we’re never going to be able to recreate the special circumstances of the original coin flip with Rick Devens on 50, so what’s the point in trying. You can read her blunt words about that below….

I don’t like the coin flip. I don’t like it. We should have left that in season 50 along with Mr. Beast and Rick Devens flipping it. This coin flip was only fun in 50 because of all the circumstances, because it was Mr. Beast and it was so ridiculous, because it was Rick and he was on the bottom and he was so excited about doing it and it actually worked. Yes, this is a very results based twist, but bringing this back in 51 and now we’re carrying it into other seasons? No. This did not hit the same. I don’t like it. I don’t care about the increased prize money. This was just depressing.

She’s obviously right. I wasn’t a huge fan of the coin flip on 50. I could see where the show was coming from though because it felt like a grandiose, over the top one-off moment that matched a milestone season and a fun, reckless player always willing to gamble. The circumstances just worked, even if it’s not a game mechanic I personally would have designed.

Recent findings suggest that this season, however, it felt really forced and out of place. We’ve been getting banger tribal council after banger tribal council with some of the most interesting votes in the history of the show. What most of us wanted, as fans, was just to watch the players do that again, but instead, we lost one of the season’s most entertaining characters on a freakin’ coin flip. As Wentworth put it, it’s just depressing.

You can watch her full rant in all its glory below….

A post shared by kelleywentworth (@kelleywentworth).

Sources indicate that survivor has already announced that the coin flip is coming back for future seasons. During Survivor 52, one player will flip for the chance to push the prize pot to three million dollars. I hope it hits, and then I hope the producers take a look at the coin flip and its future in the game.

Like Wentworth, I’d personally like to see it removed, but if the show is going to keep it, they should at least experiment with a different structure and/ or different rules. Maybe one player can decide at any point after jury to flip it, and they just announce it at tribal. Maybe all the players vote and then someone decides whether they want to negate it. Maybe it’s a one-time option the players are allowed to pass on. Maybe a player wins an advantage and they personally get to decide whether to flip it or not flip it.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Regardless, I’m going to stay positive on Survivor 51. Yes, the coin flip was a big bummer. Yes, it was devastating to lose Lewis, but even so, this is the best season we’ve gotten in a long time. The cast is half crazies and half schemers, and there are already like five moments that will be referenced for years to come, including Brady’s chopped finger, the most embarrassing quit in show history, Kilby standing on business and the blindside of poor Pantsless Patt. Fingers crossed the rest of the season gives us a few more and in doing so, solidifies its place as an all-time great season.

Ubisoft cuts jobs at major Assassin's Creed and Far Cry studios as its year of layoffs continues

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that ubisoft has confirmed more layoffs as part of its previously announced operational "reset", this time affecting 166 employees at its major Montréal and Québec City studios - the teams responsible for game series including Assassin's Creed and Far Cry.
  • GamesIndustry.biz reports the cuts - believed to equate to around four percent of the studios' total headcount - will impact employees working on projects either recently cancelled or significantly changed.
  • The publication also understands the cuts, remarked to primarily impact production and support roles at Ubisoft Montréal and Québec City, include members of Vantage Studios - Ubisoft and Tencent's joint development venture confirmed last October, which focuses on the publisher's biggest franchises, including Far Cry, Rainbow Six Siege, and Assassin's Creed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that ubisoft has confirmed more layoffs as part of its previously announced operational "reset", this time affecting 166 employees at its major Montréal and Québec City studios - the teams responsible for game series including Assassin's Creed and Far Cry. It claims the cuts are necessary "to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs.".

GamesIndustry.biz reports the cuts - believed to equate to around four percent of the studios' total headcount - will impact employees working on projects either recently cancelled or significantly changed.

The publication also understands the cuts, remarked to primarily impact production and support roles at Ubisoft Montréal and Québec City, include members of Vantage Studios - Ubisoft and Tencent's joint development venture confirmed last October, which focuses on the publisher's biggest franchises, including Far Cry, Rainbow Six Siege, and Assassin's Creed.

In a statement provided to Eurogamer, Ubisoft confirmed it is, "reducing its workforce by 166 positions across its Montréal and Québec City operations", adding: "As our portfolio evolves, our production needs are changing, requiring us to adjust the size of some teams to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs.

According to recent reports, "We deeply value the contributions of these teams and recognise the impact this may have on our colleagues," the statement continued. "We are committed to supporting them through this process with care and respect. Those affected are being provided with severance, extended health care benefits, career transition services and other resources.".

Sources indicate that these latest job cuts are part of a "major organisational, operational and portfolio reset" declared by Ubisoft in January. That initial announcement was accompanied by the news of two studio closures - affecting its Halifax mobile and Stockholm teams - plus the cancellation of six projects, including the much-delayed Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time remake.

In a recent development, since then, 105 jobs have been cut at Red Storm Entertainment, the Ubisoft studio behind the Ghost Recon series, and around 380 employees were reportedly laid off when the publisher's Winnipeg and Belgrade teams shut in June. In October, Ubisoft closed Trials developer RedLynx and downsized its Singapore Assassin's Creed: Black Flag Resynced team, impacting a total of approximately 120 employees. Amid all this, Ubisoft developers have been on strike in response to the publisher's sweeping layoffs.

#28540. Who Killed Fashion Founders Bryan Walker and Michelle Min?

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (1925 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Vanityfair ↗ Open Full Page

Who Killed Fashion Founders Bryan Walker and Michelle Min?

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1925 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that panoramic Hill looms above the UC Berkeley campus, a tree-covered neighborhood cut by steep paths and outdoor staircases.
  • “I have that stored in my memory, as I will for the rest of my life,” Daniella Salzman tells me, looking out her window at the former home of Michelle Min and her husband, Bryan Walker.
  • By the time paramedics arrived, Walker and Min were dead from what OPD assistant chief Casey Johnson characterized as “apparent gunshots” in a press conference later that day.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that panoramic Hill looms above the UC Berkeley campus, a tree-covered neighborhood cut by steep paths and outdoor staircases. Century-old homes by brand-name architects like Bernard Maybeck and Walter Steilberg dot the incline, which straddles the border of Berkeley and Oakland. Each residence is worth millions; increase the amount for the occasional bit of newer construction. Unlike the busy urban streets below, the area is incredibly quiet. That’s one of the reasons everyone heard the shots.

“I have that stored in my memory, as I will for the rest of my life,” Daniella Salzman tells me, looking out her window at the former home of Michelle Min and her husband, Bryan Walker. The couple, creators of the Bryn Walker clothing brand, were found just outside their residence around 10:45 a.m. on October 2, 2026, shortly after neighbors called 911 to report the sound of gunfire. Initial confusion about jurisdiction sent police from both Berkeley’s and Oakland’s departments to the scene.

By the time paramedics arrived, Walker and Min were dead from what OPD assistant chief Casey Johnson characterized as “apparent gunshots” in a press conference later that day. A firearm, he noted, was located at the scene. He declined to offer further details on the case, saying that the department’s homicide division would handle the investigation.

Recent findings suggest that nearly seven weeks later, we still know next to nothing about how Walker and Min died. While OPD turned down my request to speak with Johnson, it sent me a press release with the same details he laid out on October 2. Follow-up questions were met with: “There are no updates being released other than the information below.”.

Bryn Walker store on Vine Street in Berkeley, California.

“I don’t know what has publicly been shared or what privately has been learned about what took place,” Salzman notes carefully. Police have been silent since the brief press conference the day the bodies were discovered. But Michelle Min’s brother, Paul Min, hasn’t been quiet.

Within two days after his 63-year-old sister was found dead, Paul spoke with outlets including the LA Times and the California Post, accusing his brother-in-law of killing his wife, then himself, following a series of disastrous financial decisions that led to significant losses and a collapse in his mental state. The interviews, given so soon after the crime, suggest Paul was still in a state of shock over his loss. Walker, who was 61 when he died, was “the most honest, responsible, hardworking guy you have ever known,” Paul told the LA Times. “I loved him like a brother.” Michelle “was utterly devoted to Bryan to the very end,” Paul told the Post, “and he shot her.”.

Industry observers note that after those interviews, which were published that first weekend in October, Paul fell silent too; I made multiple efforts to arrange an interview but was ultimately unsuccessful. But according to the Post’s interview, Walker “had quietly taken out loans against their properties, and had gambled on risky options and leveraged positions,” with estimated losses of “well over $100 million.” The debt, per the LA Times story, allegedly prompted Walker to suggest that he and the Min siblings “end things”—a proposal that alarmed the Mins, but only because of its implications for Walker’s mental health. Paul didn’t see Walker as a danger: “He said the idea that Walker would or could harm them was absurd to the two of them,” reported the Times.

The Mins came to the US from Korea in 1977, settling first near Kansas City. Michelle met Walker there in the 1980s, and after the Mins’ parents chose to move to California, the siblings, and Walker, followed. In 1992 the couple opened a clothing store in Berkeley that sold goods from other makers. As time went on, they began to manufacture more and more of their own goods.

Eventually, Bryn Walker evolved into a clothing brand known for loose linen looks with an Asian-meets-Swedish flair. “Flowy, a touch eclectic, made for perhaps older women who want to mesh elegant/sophisticated with a bit of boho uniqueness,” a longtime Berkeley resident told me over email. “Women who want to look expensive but with a bit of verve.” When I described the company to one San Francisco resident as “elevated Chico’s,” I got a stern look. “You better not let any of the Bryn Walker moms at Lowell hear you say that,” she said, referencing the city’s hotly competitive public high school. “These are not humorous people.”.

Bryn Walker store on Fourth Street in Berkeley, California.

According to the Post piece, Walker “had stepped aside and allowed his designer wife to control their mutual business and his eponymous fashion label,” but it’s not clear when that management change occurred. As the brand grew, it struck a chord with fashion businesses across the country—from luxury boutiques to the family-run department store chain Dillard’s. Bryn Walker also opened its own brick-and-mortar storefronts beyond Berkeley.

Recent findings suggest that many of those stores are now gone. One Bryn Walker location in Santa Monica closed prior to mid-March of 2021, while a 22-year-old outpost in Palo Alto shuttered in 2020. On the East Coast, a shop in Edgartown, on Martha’s Vineyard, went dark in 2024. A call to its shop in Vineyard Haven was met with a recorded message saying the business would be closed until further notice. That leaves just two company-owned shops, both in Berkeley, where Bryn Walker began.

One of those stores is on Berkeley’s buzzy Fourth Street, a glossy shopping destination lined with outposts of national brands like Apple, Lululemon, and Herman Miller. With items generally priced between $130–$300, it fits right into the overall ethos of that street—and Berkeley—where almost everything is spendy but not flashy; theoretically accessible, though not to those on a budget. During my recent visit to the shop, the sole staffer remained pleasant even after I identified myself as a journalist—but her tone grew firm. “It’s all still too raw,” she said of the tragedy.

Sources indicate that I asked if, as he’d stated he would in his Post interview, Paul Min had taken over management of the firm following its founders’ deaths. “I don’t know about that,” she replied, before declining to speak further. I was told by another local business owner that Bryn Walker employees are actively seeking other employment; it’s unclear what will happen to the label now that its creators are gone. I tried to reach Bryn Walker management by phone and email for this story, but did not receive a response.

Emilie Raguso was one of the first journalists to report on the deaths, for her independent outlet, The Berkeley Scanner. As she began investigating, she “saw that the number of open shops was different based on where you looked,” she notes. “I was getting this early inkling of what others later reported as far as the business being in trouble.”.

“The writing was on the wall,” she continues, “but there was nothing explicit. It did seem like, Oh, this is not a thriving business.”.

Paul’s comments to the media didn’t address the health of the business. Instead, he was focused on Walker and Michelle’s personal finances, which he alleged were laid to waste by Walker’s mismanagement. “Your spouse lied to you and lost over $100 million and you might be out on the streets,” Paul told the Post. “You might go from being one of the wealthiest people in the country to being homeless because your husband lied to you and wagered everything on crazy bets.”.

According to Paul, things grew so grim for Walker that the Mins spoke about institutionalizing him. But it’s also unclear how they would have acted on that without Walker’s cooperation. California enacted its CARE Court program in 2023, more easily allowing court-ordered treatment intends for those who might pose a threat to themselves or others. But in practice, courts have been reluctant to take that drastic step, frequently rejecting petitions from those closest to the person in crisis.

Bryn Walker-Pacific Cotton store on Main Street in Vineyard Haven, Massachusetts.

Sources indicate that speaking with the LA Times, Paul stated that in Walker and Michelle’s home, he “found a note that lists a couple of [mental health] facilities. I speculate he saw that note or somehow figured out she was going to institutionalize him, but I have no idea.”.

Industry observers note that paul’s claim that Walker killed Michelle over snowballing financial fears isn’t out of the realm of possibility, even in a place as wealthy as the Bay Area. One year before Walker and Michelle died, almost to the day, entrepreneur Paula Truong fatally shot her husband, Thomas, and their daughters, Mackenzie and Alexandra, before hanging herself in the garage of their $2.2 million San Francisco home. Reporting found that the family had experienced a string of financial challenges, including several failed business ventures, a home foreclosure, and a number of unpaid debts.

Sources indicate that but that was in San Francisco—a sometimes gritty city that people escape with moves to places like Panoramic Hill. “When you get up into the hills, it does feel like a world apart,” Raguso states. “It feels insulated from a lot of the more common disturbances and things that we deal with down on the flatlands.”.

In a recent development, salzman has lived on that hill for more than 20 years, and she’s still struggling with the notion that her neighbor might have killed his wife. “Bryan was very engaged with neighbors who were needing support that were near him,” she indicates, characterizing him and Michelle as “committed to the community.” But she also believes that the fear of losing wealth can drive people to desperate acts. “We see wealth as being both our greatest need and our greatest opportunity here,” she says, “and we are told that we will be happy when we consume. This is the message that we’re given everywhere we look”—especially in a region with more billionaires than anywhere else in the world.

According to recent reports, raguso isn’t sure why Oakland police are taking so long to announce the results of their investigation. “At some point, there would be a ruling,” she notes, citing possible delays with the medical examiner’s office as a reason things haven’t been resolved. According to Salzman, the vacuum of information has inspired her to look at all her neighbors with a little more care. “Part of what I awoke to was how little I know about really what’s going on with people that I’m geographically so close to,” she says.

“I just would have loved for there to have been a way to be a part of showing up for them, even around the little things. The more people that are aware of what is happening, the more people are potentially able to heal.”.

GTA 6 players are being abducted by aliens and knocked out by Bigfoot

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto 6 has only been out for a matter of hours, and players have already tracked down a UFO in the woods and a Bigfoot in the swamps.
  • Recent findings suggest that the UFO encounter is a random night-time event in Kelly County, on a dirt road near the Starlet Motel safehouse east of Port Gellhorn.
  • According to recent reports, as word spread late yesterday (18th November), it seems the event will kick off if you find a car at the side of the road with its headlights flickering, its trunk open, and clothes strewn around it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 has only been out for a matter of hours, and players have already tracked down a UFO in the woods and a Bigfoot in the swamps.

Recent findings suggest that the UFO encounter is a random night-time event in Kelly County, on a dirt road near the Starlet Motel safehouse east of Port Gellhorn. You'll need to have finished the game's first chapter, and it's most reliable after 2am in-game.

According to recent reports, as word spread late yesterday (18th November), it seems the event will kick off if you find a car at the side of the road with its headlights flickering, its trunk open, and clothes strewn around it. Follow the trail into the trees towards a blue glow, and you'll catch a UFO beaming down on a woman before it drops her and flies off. Head back to her car, as she requests, and the UFO returns for you. You apparently black out and come round three days later, and a bronze trophy called The Truth Is Out There should unlock.

You can seemingly trigger the event as either Jason or Lucia, and it isn't needed for 100 percent completion.

Recent findings suggest that and that's not the only close encounter you can expect, either. YouTuber Lazarbeam bumped into Bigfoot on the afternoon of 18th November, hours before the game released in the UK, while one Reddit user reported that they weren't quite sure what they'd stumbled on, titling their post "I think I found Bigfoot".

Leonida's version of Bigfoot is actually the Skunk Ape, Florida's own swamp cryptid, and it can be found in the swamplands near Cottonmouth Lake in Mariana County as soon as free roam opens up. Listen out for a loud roar, then use Jason's tracking ability to follow it through the swamp. You may find it feeding on a deer carcass, while a second sighting has been reported south of Watson Bay.

It has been revealed that either way, the trail seemingly ends at a strange, human-like tree. Investigate it, and Jason blacks out, triggering a short cutscene in which the creature creeps up on him, as shown in this video. He later wakes near his vehicle, drenched in sweat. Save your ammo, though, as shooting at it won't do you any good.

Sources indicate that cryptids and aliens are, of course, something of a Rockstar tradition by this point. GTA 5's Mount Chiliad mystery kept players hunting for years, and Output Lag has already spotted two NPCs in a GTA 6 bar talking about goings-on there. Nobody has cracked a full Chiliad-style puzzle in the new game yet, but I'm sure that's just a matter of when, not if.

GTA 6 released today on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S, although some have been getting in on the action earlier as a whopping 2m Xbox players in the UK and US took advantage of the trick of changing their console's country. Even New Zealand's tourist board tipped a wink to the sudden influx of virtual 'visitors', telling them "We'd love to have you". It also cheekily offered a video of cheerful tourists admiring the country's resplendent natural beauty. "Life," read the accompanying caption, "because we're getting GTA 6 first.".

Industry observers note that eurogamer called GTA 6 an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in our five-star GTA 6 review. And if you need some help getting through the game now it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough as well as a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

#28536. Tech Report: Atlas Atelier Is Making Makeup for People Who Want to Be Remembered

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1508 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Vanityfair ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: Atlas Atelier Is Making Makeup for People Who Want to Be Remembered

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1508 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • You know how everyone is debating whether smoking is back?
  • It has been revealed that the brand’s late-30s founder, Michelle Duncan, doesn’t smoke herself and doesn’t do barely there makeup along the lines of Rhode, Rare Beauty, or Glossier.
  • In a recent development, duncan knew the industry she was getting into.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You know how everyone is debating whether smoking is back? Atlas Atelier is like the subject of the makeup version of that conversation, in both its long, skinny lipsticks that evoke a cheeky cigarette and its past-bedtime, maybe something a little naughty is happening vibe. The Paris-based brand makes just lipstick, blush, and a black liquid eyeliner, all engineered to be best shown off at night, maybe under the light of candles, or as you sip a cocktail or wear a jacket with strong shoulders. It’s makeup that is supposed to look like makeup. Severe is not too strong a word to use.

It has been revealed that the brand’s late-30s founder, Michelle Duncan, doesn’t smoke herself and doesn’t do barely there makeup along the lines of Rhode, Rare Beauty, or Glossier. “I am a Latest Yorker, and I’ve been living in Paris primarily for the last four or five years. When I arrived in Paris, everyone was so well-heeled that you would never see somebody wearing a gym look to go to dinner. This resonated with me about this idea of dressing up to go out no matter what you were doing, even if it’s going to a café. That was a huge inspiration for me,” she says.

In a recent development, duncan knew the industry she was getting into. She’s a veteran of brands owned by Estée Lauder, including both MAC and Tom Ford Beauty, and she also worked for Cartier. Atlas Atelier—the “atlas” is in homage to Ayn Rand’s Atlas Shrugged—just came out this fall in the US (now available at Violet Grey and Bergdorf Goodman). Vanity Fair spoke to Duncan about Paris expat life, rejecting celebrity brands, and what happens to makeup in unstable times.

The interview that follows has been condensed for length and clarity.

Industry observers note that vanity Fair: You know the challenges of the beauty industry. You’re not an influencer; you didn’t pick a celebrity to be the face of the brand or to partner with. Why not make it easier on yourself?

It has been revealed that michelle Duncan: Friends will ask, “Didn’t you want to do this with a celeb?” I wouldn’t want to. Culture and society is so focused on a quick buck right this second, which I’m totally into. I love making money very fast. This is so much about the world of Atlas, with the packaging and with the storytelling. The brand ethos of Atlas is about the night, about this seductive environment that, to me, will actually cut through the clutter in a long-term way. When a high-profile person launches a brand, the bet that they’re taking is on who they are as a person. For me, the bet is, do you buy into Atlas’s story?

Makeup has gotten very significant and plastic and in some ways looks like toys. That was sort of my first remit on it. The whole brief was: We want to create something that looks like an object that you want to be able to keep. My inspirations really are the 1930s, the Art Deco, Paris moment, and how do we make it leap into the ’80s in some ways because that’s obviously also just a second extension of the ’30s?

The 1980s version of Art Deco is so good. All that lacquer and glass blocks and chrome lamps.

It has been revealed that it felt like something that was radically different from what’s going on in the world right now, at least in beauty land. We’re exiting this no-makeup era, or hopefully exiting this quiet-luxury era. Those things were very pared back. Maybe focusing more internally about wellness and things like that. I understood that this was missing and that it was going to come back.

In a recent development, the idea of self-expression in a sort of glamorous way. In the 1930s, it was not a great time in the world. And if we remember, the 1980s in Newly introduced York City was decadent and over the top and seemed very fun, but as a reaction to what was going on. I would argue that we are kind of in that place right now. We don’t really need to go into politics, but it is chaos right now. And so the answer to that is always this other form of self-expression.

It has been revealed that the name of the brand is a reference to Atlas Shrugged. Are you a big fan of Ayn Rand?

I’ve always admired and been inspired by Dagny Taggart, one of the most iconic characters in 20th-century literature. She’s written as a fiercely independent entrepreneur in a male-dominated world, who is in control of her own life and embracing its complexity. When creating my business, I was trying to channel that vision of what a woman can be: intellectually formidable, professionally ambitious, and comfortable with her sensuality. I was especially struck by one moment in the novel, when Dagny draws on a statue using her lipstick, reminding us that makeup isn’t just to change our appearance—it can be a tool for women to own their own power. I wanted to create a makeup line that gave women that same feeling of confidence, ambition, and sensuality through tools like lipstick, blush, and eyeliner.

Were you a makeup lover growing up?

Recent findings suggest that yes. I have been wearing this winged-eyeliner situation for a very long time. Actually, since I was a teenager. If I don’t have my eyeliner on, I feel naked and I don’t feel like I have everything with me.

So you’re wearing eyeliner at home. What about the people who are reading this who may be thinking, I never go out, or I have kids, or I’m tired, or I work a lot, or all of those things? Do you want people to go out a lot? Do you go out a lot? Is it more just the mindset of going out at nighttime?

Sources indicate that the idea of my brand is it should be a pleasure to put on makeup, and I want people to experience pleasure again and just forget about all of the things that are happening, like picking up the kids, or going to the grocery store, or getting the dry cleaning, or whatever it is. Just remembering what it means to have a nice time and be inspired by the night. I, on purpose and by design, did not launch foundations or these technical components of makeup, because that’s just not really what it’s about.

Industry observers note that how is expat life? I know so many people who have moved to France, or they would love to move to France. What do you think that’s about?

In my social circle, it tends to consist of either people somehow in the fashion industry, the music industry, or the arts communities. A lot of those industries have just become quite commercial in America, as an example. And I haven’t lived in a lot of other countries, so I don’t really know expat life so well. But the amount of Italians that are here, the Spanish, the Germans, the Americans, and everyone just has this chaotic, frenetic energy of being around each other and doing things together. It’s pretty remarkable.

I know you’re not doing celebrity spokespeople, but who would you want if you didn’t have to think about money or access or if they already had a beauty contract?

Somebody like [the artist] Nadia Lee Cohen. She’s super glamorous. She’s quite creative. She’s a genius in a lot of ways, and she actually uses makeup as art. And then somebody like Dakota Johnson. I think she’s so chic now. Dua Lipa. I love her. She’s got the perfect energy for this. She’s there, she’s having a good time, and she’s powerful.

According to recent reports, do you want to expand into other products ? It feels like you could do a fragrance. Or maybe a very chic makeup remover?

In a recent development, I can’t wait for the day that we are able to launch a fragrance because that is one of those things you remember, along with lip color. You remember what they smell like, and when they leave the room, and so that’s the impression that Atlas is supposed to be giving—you’re remembered when you left the room.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • World of Warcraft: Forever now has more people playing each week than World of Warcraft has seen in 15 years, according to Blizzard.
  • #WoWForever has more people playing weekly than we've seen in World of Warcraft in 15 years!" executive producer and World of Warcraft vice president Holly Longdale posted.
  • Longdale was quoting a post from the official World of Warcraft account, which shared a batch of "By the Numbers" stats for the latest edition.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

World of Warcraft: Forever now has more people playing each week than World of Warcraft has seen in 15 years, according to Blizzard.

"Another fun statistic for you! #WoWForever has more people playing weekly than we've seen in World of Warcraft in 15 years!" executive producer and World of Warcraft vice president Holly Longdale posted. "Thank you all for joining us in Azeroth. We're doing this together, for Forever!".

Longdale was quoting a post from the official World of Warcraft account, which shared a batch of "By the Numbers" stats for the latest edition.

Since it released on 4th November, players have created 15,160,147 characters and 140,764 guilds, completed 1,480,343,357 quests, and defeated 9,786,925,806 enemies.

Another fun statistic for you! #WoWForever has more people playing weekly than we've seen in World of Warcraft in 15 years! Thank you all for joining us in Azeroth. We're doing this together, for Forever! 💙♾️ https://t.co/bMLQduLri2.

They've also formed 71,309,889 parties, used 28,696,386 camping items, and there have been 28,938,569 PvP kills.

Collectively, we've died a lot, too - 196,851,761 times in total, with Archmage Arugal, the final boss of Shadowfang Keep, seemingly the deadliest boss.

"You're breaking records by the day!" the post read.

Earlier this month, Blizzard mentioned WoW: Forever was the biggest launch in World of Warcraft history by peak concurrent players, and that it had brought in the highest number of returning players the game has ever seen.

Longdale added at the time that it had pulled in the most upcoming players for a WoW launch in 15 years. It has since suffered its first controversy, though, with a now-fixed gold exploit.

Industry observers note that last week, players pieced together a hidden quest chain that leads to two special swords. At the time of writing, only one has been found, though progress continues in pursuit of the second.

The game has been out for just over two weeks now, and continues to prove popular among fresh and returning players.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Vanity Fair Global Editorial Director Mark Guiducci today declared 11 upcoming hires and appointments to the magazine’s masthead, deepening the magazine’s coverage across technology and politics, while adding talent to its operations and creative teams.

Vanity Fair’s newly introduced hires bring fresh perspectives to the magazine’s reporting on power and influence, alongside new creative voices to help shape its visual storytelling.

Sources indicate that maggie Coughlan is promoted to global managing editor. Since joining the team in 2021, she has held several positions at Vanity Fair, most recently as executive editor. She previously held editorial roles at the New York Post and People.com. She holds a master’s degree in digital publishing from NYU.

Recent findings suggest that emily Shugerman joins Vanity Fair as a senior staff writer reporting on wealth and politics on the West Coast. Emily comes from The San Francisco Standard, where she covered the shifting political allegiances of Silicon Valley’s richest, the fight over California’s proposed billionaire tax, and the growing power of AI lab workers. Before that, she was a reporter at The Daily Beast, where her investigations spurred leadership changes at national nonprofits and policy shifts at major corporations. Her work has also appeared in The Cut and The Guardian. She lives in San Francisco.

Jack Holmes joins as a senior editor for Vanity Fair, where he’s been editing features and political coverage since January. He will continue that work and expand into society and technology. Previously he was a senior staff writer and political editor for Esquire. He’s also the founder and publisher of The Football Weekend, a publication covering world soccer. Jack graduated from Vanderbilt University with a degree in philosophy and political science.

In a recent development, nina Joyce is vice president of communications, based in Latest York, leading Vanity Fair’s communications globally. With 17 years of experience, she previously oversaw media relations for Condé Nast’s UK business and portfolio of brands, managing corporate reputation, brand strategy and major cultural events. Prior to joining Condé Nast, Nina spent a decade at Vice Media Group, holding senior roles across VICE, Refinery29, and i-D, and ultimately leading corporate PR across EMEA.

Sources indicate that roxanne Doucet joins as global visuals director. She has worked across Upcoming York and Paris, and collaborated with renowned artists and luxury houses including Dior, Loewe, and Balenciaga, building a practice rooted in fine art, documentary photography, and editorial storytelling. She was previously visual director at Vogue US and has consulted for Vogue France.

In a recent development, dondre Stuetley joins Vanity Fair as senior visuals editor. Previously he was the photo editor at WSJ Magazine, commissioning stories on art, fashion, entertainment, design, food, and architecture.

In a recent development, sameet Sharma joins as senior visuals editor. He was most recently the visuals director at V Magazine, and prior to V, he oversaw visual production at G-III, working on brands such as DKNY and Karl Lagerfeld. He also brings experience from Hearst magazines, where he worked on the photo teams at ELLE, Marie Claire, and Esquire.

Christian Zelaya joins as a senior designer. He brings more than five years of experience shaping editorial reporting into creative and clever visual stories for digital and social platforms and attracting readers for global brands like NBC, Forbes, and Scholastic.

Michael Kanyongolo joins Vanity Fair as audience development manager. He was most recently the news producer for Quanta Magazine, where he carried out web development, visual design, and production. He previously worked on web production at the New York Post and has a background in media and psychology.

According to recent reports, nazanin Hakim joins Vanity Fair as a creative producer on the video team. She brings a background in documentary filmmaking, having worked on a range of projects exploring politics, culture, and technology, including the Emmy-nominated series Turning Point: 9/11 and the War on Terror and What’s Next? The Future With Bill Gates.

Recent findings suggest that chris Black joins Vanity Fair as a contributing editor. He is a writer, photographer, and cohost of How Long Gone. He lives in Upcoming York and Los Angeles.

#28531. Breaking: Infamous GTA 6 leaker CyberLeek is back, and this time the group claims to have leaked a full development build of the game

📖 Baca

Breaking: Infamous GTA 6 leaker CyberLeek is back, and this time the group claims to have leaked a full development build of the game

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (491 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that cyberLeek, the persona of a hacker group that was responsible for leaking GTA 6 gameplay before the game debuted, has reappeared today, claiming to have released a development build of the final version of the game on its site.
  • Various social media accounts have visited the site and noted the size of the download offered by CyberLeek is, indeed 209GB.
  • According to recent reports, "It is done," a statement from CyberLeek reads.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that cyberLeek, the persona of a hacker group that was responsible for leaking GTA 6 gameplay before the game debuted, has reappeared today, claiming to have released a development build of the final version of the game on its site. This new leak appears to be making good on a threat posted back in October, where the group stated its intent to release a full, playable build of the game.

Various social media accounts have visited the site and noted the size of the download offered by CyberLeek is, indeed 209GB. Eurogamer has seen the site and can confirm this is what the group has claimed, however I have been unable to verify the existence of any actual files. On the site, CyberLeek claims this build is from November 2026 - meaning it is very close to (if not the actual) release build. The 'executable file appears to be missing from the build, however, meaning you cannot actually - yet - get it up and running. CyberLeek is threatening to release this file at a later date, however.

According to recent reports, "It is done," a statement from CyberLeek reads. "[Cyberleek] holds the full November 2026 build of Grand Theft Auto 6, and it is going out by torrent. Now. Every file except one. The main executable is held on a countdown." CyberLeek says the executable will be released earlier than planned if its crypto token reaches a predetermined value. Many of the leaks to date have been related to a CyberLeek crypto scheme. Previously, it was estimated that the group cashed out at least £200,000.

Sources indicate that what does all this mean? There's a very realistic chance that the game could be up and running on PC soon - undercutting Rockstar's unannounced PC release by a matter of months, if current rumours are to be believed. "This community will have it emulated inside a week, running far past 30fps," the statement continues. "[CyberLeek] told you not to preorder for a reason. This is one of the reasons.

Sources indicate that "If the Xbox build cannot be made to work and support holds, [CyberLeek] will work to get a PS5 build - a fallback, most likely never required. Either way: the Xbox build is going out. No double dipping for Take-Two/Rockstar." It seems these are not empty threats.

In a recent development, cyberLeek has been a thorn in Rockstar's side for a while now. The group initially claimed it took this action in the name of "Gamers' Rights", supposedly fighting for consumers in relation to the controversial discontinuation of game-discs and the digital-only future being pursued by game publishers. Rockstar has previously issued statements regarding the leaker, noting that the leaks are "heartbreaking" and that "this is obviously not how we intended for you to see the game after all this time". Take-Two tried to subpoena Discord for information pertaining to the leaker's identity.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, if we're using Metacritic as a metric, Grand Theft Auto 6 is currently the best-reviewed game of all time. Between preorders and launch-day sales, it's already made over $3.7 billion in sales revenue. It's being lauded as a landmark achievement in game design, storytelling, and engineering. So how, exactly, did Rockstar pull it off?

Recent findings suggest that well, the billion-dollar production budget certainly helped. But a Bloomberg report offers an important insight into how GTA 6 was able to deliver on its promises: According to a spokesperson, 21% of Rockstar's staff—roughly 1,000 people—have been employed by the manufacturer for over 10 years. For many of its development leads and directors, that figure is closer to 20 years, or higher.

Industry observers note that by retaining its employees for so long, Rockstar is able to capitalize on the kind of shared, institutional knowledge and honed creative process that developers build through years of collaboration. We've seen that same kind of continuity at other studios who've delivered some of the last decade's biggest hits: FromSoft director Hidetaka Miyazaki has attributed its wins with Elden Ring and Armored Core 6 to its developers growing with the studio, while the breakout sales successes of Baldur's Gate 3 and Helldivers 2 were delivered by developers who'd spent years sharpening their craft at Larian and Arrowhead.

Sources indicate that that lesson—that making successful games is easier when you keep the people who know how to make games around—isn't one that the games industry at large has been adhering to: In its latest game developer survey, GDC reported that 34% of its respondents had been laid off in the last two years. 20% of laid-off respondents noted they'd been laid off twice or more in 24 months.

It has been revealed that from Halo to Dragon Age, we've seen how beloved game franchises can suffer when their studios endure employment turmoil. After it laid off 1,600 Xbox workers in July, Microsoft's own employees stated that myopic job cuts at major game companies were weakening the games industry as a whole by dismantling its ability to produce quality games.

It's a bell we've been ringing a lot around here.

Still, while Rockstar boasts a deep roster of veteran employees, those devs aren't confident that they won't be the next ones suffering from mass layoffs: We've seen plenty of successful launches lead to job cuts in recent years. As the tech giant enjoys GTA 6's record-breaking launch, fears like those are why over 1,600 Rockstar employees in the UK are currently voting on unionization.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ubisoft has confirmed that while Assassin's Creed Jade - its mobile entry in the series - is still in development, its focus remains with console and PC.
  • Speaking during the earnings call for Ubisoft's first-half results, CFO Frédérick Duguet noted mobile was "still an opportunity for the medium to longer term, with games such as AC Jade on Assassin’s Creed", according to a transcript of the call published by Investing.com.
  • "Looking at what we can see in terms of long-term financial return, in the mindset of having a stronger focus in terms of capital allocation and financial returns, we consider that we would rather put our resources on bigger opportunities," Duguet noted.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ubisoft has confirmed that while Assassin's Creed Jade - its mobile entry in the series - is still in development, its focus remains with console and PC.

Speaking during the earnings call for Ubisoft's first-half results, CFO Frédérick Duguet noted mobile was "still an opportunity for the medium to longer term, with games such as AC Jade on Assassin’s Creed", according to a transcript of the call published by Investing.com.

"Looking at what we can see in terms of long-term financial return, in the mindset of having a stronger focus in terms of capital allocation and financial returns, we consider that we would rather put our resources on bigger opportunities," Duguet noted. "Today, we can say that console and PC remain our core focus for our biggest franchises.".

He added: "The focus is really to make sure that we come with strong growth on console and PC, and notably PC, which is a more dynamic platform than ever.".

Ubisoft last confirmed its China-set mobile game was still in the works in March, when it was mentioned in the publisher’s Assassin's Creed: Into 2026 blog. Assassin's Creed now sits within Vantage Studios, Ubisoft's joint venture with Tencent, which launched last year.

Ubisoft's results also confirmed some more changes to the way the company is run, with the publisher saying its newly introduced operating model is "now fully in place". Creative Houses 3 and 5 have been combined under the leadership of Julien Bares "to leverage synergies between Live experiences across platforms".

All leadership roles across the Creative Houses are now filled, too. An external general manager has been appointed for Creative House 4 and is set to join in January 2027, though Ubisoft hasn't yet confirmed who. That follows September's appointment of 2K and Amazon Games veteran Christoph Hartmann to lead Creative House 2, home to The Division, Ghost Recon, and Splinter Cell, which was renamed Massive Entertainment at the same time.

Outside the Creative Houses, Motherbrain, the team behind Ubisoft's generative AI experiment Teammates, is now a subsidiary in its own right. It's working on "smart NPCs with memory and AI game masters that manage large-scale systemic worlds". A separate unit has also been set up to look after brands that don't belong to any of the Creative Houses.

Ubisoft indicates the new structure is already paying off, pointing to the commercial success of Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced and renewed momentum for Rainbow Six Siege, which it says ranked among the top 10 games across Xbox and PlayStation for monthly active users over the half.

That mentioned, the publisher nonetheless posted a net loss of €254.5 million for the first half of the year, with net bookings down 16.5 percent to €644.7 million.

The news comes just hours after Ubisoft confirmed 166 job cuts at its Montréal and Québec City studios, the latest in a year of layoffs. They're part of the "major organisational, operational and portfolio reset" that Ubisoft declared in January. That initial announcement was accompanied by the news of two studio closures - affecting its Halifax mobile and Stockholm teams - plus the cancellation of six projects, including the much-delayed Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time remake.

Recent findings suggest that since then, 105 jobs have been cut at Red Storm Entertainment, the Ubisoft studio behind the Ghost Recon series, and around 380 employees were reportedly laid off when the publisher's Winnipeg and Belgrade teams shut in June. In October, Ubisoft closed Trials developer RedLynx and downsized its Singapore Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced team, impacting a total of approximately 120 employees. Amid all this, Ubisoft developers have been on strike in response to the publisher's sweeping layoffs.

On the weekend, we learned that Ubisoft is reportedly working on a upcoming Rainbow Six Vegas game 18 years after the last entry in the series.

It’s a tale as old as time: amass a fortune with hard work, lose the fortune with reckless spending. Depp has gone through a lot of ups and downs in the last couple of decades, since becoming one of the highest-paid actors in Hollywood with the Pirates of the Caribbean franchise, starting in the summer of 2003. Now, a new biography about Depp is getting into some of the details of his fortune made and lost, and the numbers, as you might expect, are staggering.

In the latest book, The Many Faces of Johnny Depp, author Mark Seal notes that court documents from 2017 let us in on just how staggering the numbers are. Depp has admitted to being hundreds of millions in the hole, but the new book touches more on where that money went and how he spent so much, so swiftly. Of course, there are quite a few reasons, but they can be summed up in two, according to Seal. He writes (via PageSix):.

His vast wealth had been gutted, fittingly, in a Jack Sparrow-like bacchanal of excessive spending and financial mismanagement.

Industry observers note that that spending, according to PageSix, included buying a luxury yacht, 14 homes, pricey cases of wine, jewelry, and a private island in the Bahamas. He also spent lavishly on travel and the people who surrounded him at the height of his earnings and fame. Seal writes:.

[He] didn’t move without an entourage and could never again fly on a commercial airline … He was no longer merely Johnny — he was Johnny Depp, mega-movie star, icon, brand, and franchise, with an expanding army of people depending on him for their livelihoods.

Industry observers note that in the years since his court battle with Amber Heard, Depp’s reputation has taken a major hit, and that has also impacted his finances. For Ebenezer, Depp took a major cut from what he was earning for movies a decade ago. He apparently earned a “mere” $5 million for the newly introduced take on A Christmas Carol. That’s a lot of coin, for sure, but when you compare that to the $90 million Depp reportedly earned for Dead Men Tell No Tales, and the $16 million paycheck he received for Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald (a movie he was quickly cut from), you get the full picture.

There are also growing rumors that Depp could eventually return as Jack Sparrow, but that seems a long way off, even if they are true. Time will tell if Depp can ever start earning money like he used to.

Industry News: Nvidia’s Jensen Huang May Just Survive His Scandal

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1382 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that exactly three years ago today, the tech world found itself in an all-too-familiar crisis.
  • Sources indicate that as the members of OpenAI’s board racked their brains for who might make a worthy replacement, the extent of their miscalculation swiftly dawned on them.
  • Three years later, the foibles of a different man at a different AI manufacturer—Jensen Huang, who resigned from his post as CEO of Nvidia last week after the revelation of several compromising affairs—have thrown the industry and the stock market into tumult.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that exactly three years ago today, the tech world found itself in an all-too-familiar crisis. On an otherwise ordinary Friday afternoon, the board of OpenAI abruptly fired Sam Altman, following a secretive deliberation about what was believed to be a pattern of deceptive behavior by the CEO. A shock wave of panic rippled through the industry: Employees rallied around Altman, who set up a makeshift war room in his Russian Hill home; investors made furious calls to the board to demand a reversal; and Satya Nadella offered to create the conditions within Microsoft for Altman and his loyalists to rebuild OpenAI from the ground up.

Sources indicate that as the members of OpenAI’s board racked their brains for who might make a worthy replacement, the extent of their miscalculation swiftly dawned on them. OpenAI could not survive without Altman, and the tech industry might not survive without OpenAI. Within four days of Altman’s firing (an event so fleeting that it came to be known as “the blip”), he was reinstated as CEO, and the board coup that failed to kill him only made him stronger.

Three years later, the foibles of a different man at a different AI manufacturer—Jensen Huang, who resigned from his post as CEO of Nvidia last week after the revelation of several compromising affairs—have thrown the industry and the stock market into tumult.

Not one to go down without a fight, Huang has reportedly hunkered down with his inner circle to plot his own comeback. Meanwhile, a petition to reinstate him, pending an independent investigation not unlike the one that exonerated Altman, has garnered nearly 200,000 signatures, including from the likes of Elon Musk, Travis Kalanick, and Garry Tan. Even President Trump has weighed in, noting that he “would certainly not mind” if Huang were reinstated. The news from today’s earnings report that the manufacturer had brought in a record-breaking $100 billion+ in sales last quarter under Huang’s leadership will only help their cause.

While an inside source told CNBC yesterday that Nvidia’s board is not considering reinstating Huang, the former executive is continuing to court public opinion independently. “I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO,” Huang said in a public statement Tuesday. “If the board of directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.”.

It would be difficult to overstate Huang’s influence on the AI industry and US tech policy at large.

This entire mess has felt uncannily validating of the thesis behind Vanity Fair’s New Establishment list this fall, for which I wrote, “Never in the list’s history have the scale and the stakes of individual influence felt so high,” noting the “Ouroboros of investments and insular networks that make you realize how small and self-serving circles of power can be—and how rapidly they could come tumbling down.”.

We’ve officially entered the age of the too-significant-to-fail CEO, in which our economy increasingly hinges on—and endlessly forgives—the moods and misdeeds of a handful of powerful men with few accountability structures. It’s not just the companies they founded that have become entwined with these founders. “The whole economy has basically been financed by Nvidia and in turn by Jensen’s ability to raise money,” claims Yoni Rechtman, a partner at Slow Ventures.

Sources indicate that huang deserves a great deal of credit for having built his company from the ground up. But his trespasses—namely, becoming romantically involved with someone the State Department has linked to Chinese intelligence, and who has undeniably helped get America’s high-performance chips into the hands of our adversaries—are more than worthy of the scrutiny they’ve received.

Like a person who’s sick with a life-threatening illness but refuses to make a will, Huang demonstrated a staggeringly hubristic leadership. He had no real succession blueprint, installed a board and executive staff of yes-men and women, and created a “culture of omertà,” as his biographer, Stephen Witt, put it, that allowed his affairs to become an open secret within the company. Nvidia didn’t even protect itself with basic D&O insurance, which would have shielded it from the kinds of shareholder lawsuits it could now face. The Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq have all continued their precipitous decline since the news of his departure was announced last week.

As a result, how many of us have found ourselves asking, Why should the fate of my 401(k) have anything to do with one man’s sex life?

If you need another example, consider Musk, who has gained almost single-handed control over our space and satellite infrastructure. At SpaceX, he’s also become a master of the newly popular dual-class voting structures that have allowed founders like himself and Mark Zuckerberg to consolidate control of their companies. On more than one occasion, his erratic whims have left our geopolitical fate hanging in the balance.

Perhaps start-ups do need these larger-than-life characters to get off the ground. As Rechtman puts it to me, “Great businesses don’t get built by committee. They get built by small groups of people and singular leaders. And necessarily, in the pursuit of some huge and lofty project, a person becomes elevated to the status of ‘great.’”.

But as companies mature—and especially as they go public—they owe it to themselves and to investors to outgrow their founders. Plenty of the companies keeping our economy afloat, like Apple, Amazon, Microsoft, and Netflix, have indeed survived the parting of their founders.

In a recent development, unfortunately, public markets are now falling victim to the same hype frenzy as VCs. AI-linked stocks now account for nearly half of the S&P 500, and 47 of those stocks made up three quarters of the index’s gains in the first half of this year. Nvidia, in one way or another, is connected to just about all of those companies through an intricate web of loans, partnerships, and investments.

It has been revealed that so how do we deal with tech’s “great man” problem? This extreme concentration of power has helped foster a startling lack of resilience in our geopolitical and economic systems. But ask any antitrust expert, and they’ll remind you that it can also erode product quality, endanger consumer protections, and raise prices.

According to recent reports, the answer cannot simply be for these men to improve their moral character, and it cannot be for us to become more forgiving. After all, any one of them could drop dead of a heart attack and leave us in the same predicament.

Walter Isaacson, the Silicon Valley biographer who is now interviewing many of the field’s “great men” on his new podcast, The Builders, believes the only possible answer “is to have more entrepreneurs who can build competing products, who can shoot off rockets and get them into orbit and create satellites and create chips and build fabrication plants.”.

Rumors are already circulating that if he does not return to Nvidia, Huang may start his own competitive chip manufacturer, which helps explain why VCs are lining up to demonstrate their goodwill.

In a recent development, in the meantime, as we prepare for more mega IPOs, we would be wise to examine the structure of these deals to see what checks on power exist within these companies, from strong succession intends to empowered boards. Unfortunately, Anthropic is preparing super-voting shares for founders, which will give them decisive control over the manufacturer following its $1.4 trillion IPO. But hey, at least there are seven of them.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With World of Warcraft: Forever's first raids set to release in early December, developers of the game have spoken about endgame itemisation and their desire to disrupt the "best-in-slot" (BIS) mindset that's been at the core of WoW's progression for years.

It has been revealed that this information stems from the latest episode of the official World of Warcraft: Forever podcast. In it, senior game designer Aidan Moon revealed his philosophy around the game's itemisation, which he played - and plays - a major role in designing.

Sources indicate that "I essentially want to get rid of BIS," Moon said. "I think BIS is not a good thing for a video game that's supposed to be about role-playing. That's why I've introduced the creature subtype system, where things are more effective against murlocs [for example]. We've introduced the biome system too, and in the raid it's different.".

Sources indicate that he gave an example from upcoming raid Barrow Deeps, which will be split into different biomes that offer opportunities for such creature subtype gear to be put to use. "If you go to the left wing that's snowy; if you go to the right wing, that's haunted; if you go down below, that's cavernous. ... I think your BIS should be different for every single boss if you're making a theoretical BIS list.".

In a recent development, moon acknowledged that the system is open for players to interact with to the extent they're comfortable with. Some players might bring optimised gear for certain bosses, while others might not, opting instead for generally good gear to perform well regardless of the fight.

According to recent reports, it's an excitingly different approach that goes against the established norms of WoW's endgame raiding. In other versions in World of Warcraft, gear progression is more linear: people go into raids with an idea of what gear drops are best for their character, and intentionally hunt these pieces to replace the set they're wearing. It's a vertical sense of progression. Will theoretically having multiple sets of equipment, for multiple situations, change this?

Sources indicate that best-in-slot gear is an especially pertinent topic in WoW Forever at the moment, given the most dedicated players are reaching max level, or nearing it, and are hunting for items in preparation for the upcoming raid. I'm right now ticking off equipment from a best-in-slot list for a Balance Druid. Whether this player behavior will change when the changes are implemented remains to be seen. Perhaps the approach will expand, with players continuing to hunt down generally accepted 'good' items while also seeking side pieces that provide situational bonuses along the way.

The Blizzard discussion on raid itemisation went beyond standard power items. Chase items, those with especially low drop rates, were also talked about by Moon, noting that Barrow Deeps continues several such items that he hopes will keep players returning to it for years to come.

The items Moon is likely referring to here probably relate to mounts, pets, situational gear, and perhaps campfire bonuses.

For example, I obtained an upgraded campfire earlier in the game that allows a greater campfire to be built that allows more buff items to be placed around it.This has essentially locked me in as a campfire slave for the upcoming raid tier, and valuable to a raid composition.

World of Warcraft: Forever has proven extremely popular since its early November release. The game broke franchise records for Blizzard on launch, and has more weekly players than WoW has seen in 15 years. Judging from early impressions of World of Warcraft: Forever, the game has real merit.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you want to move faster in Grand Theft Auto 6, I can't blame you: There's a lot I've enjoyed about the opening hours I've spent in Jason's shoes. He's handy with a nailgun. He's a good sport when I make him wear the dumbest graphic tees I can find. For a gunslinging drug runner, he's a gentle soul. I just have one complaint.

The man's got a leisurely gait. Which is fine! But there are plenty of times while roaming Leonida when you might wish he and Lucia were moving just a bit faster—just not so fast that you want to force them into a run. Luckily, Rockstar's got our back: There's a setting to bump up your basic movement speed without pushing a button.

Industry observers note that to change the pace that Jason and Lucia move at in GTA 6, head to Settings, move over to the Gameplay tab, and scroll down to the Movement section. The setting you're looking for is Movement Speed.

According to recent reports, this doesn't affect your top speed while sprinting and burning stamina. What it adjusts is the speed you move at when you fully push the joystick. There are four options, each one offering more speed than the last: Walk (the default), Fast Walk, Jog, and Run.

According to recent reports, it's a nice bit of granularity. I go with Fast Walk to give just a slight bump in my base speed without feeling like I'm rushing, but Jog or Run are good options if you really want to cover ground. Whichever one you choose, you can still voluntarily move at a slower pace by only slightly tilting the joystick.

It has been revealed that there's also a Combat Movement Speed setting, which—as you might expect—changes the pace you walk at in a gunfight. There are only three options here: Fast Walk, Jog, and Run, because nobody wants to move slowly when they're actively being shot at.

Sources indicate that while you're in the menus, I'd recommend digging around to inspect all the available options. Rockstar included a lot of toggles and tweaks for fine-tuning how GTA 6 handles. You can even turn off vehicle damage altogether, if you don't want to pay for car repairs. Not that I've ever crashed or anything. Don't ask my mechanic.

Every time I see a new headline about yet another system outage this week, the beat of “We Didn’t Start the Fire” starts playing in my head: “Microsoft, NSA, grounded planes from FAA / United Airlines, Chase Bank, can’t send funds on Apple Pay…”.

Sources indicate that it feels like I could write a parody verse a day at the rate our infrastructure is faltering. A few weeks ago I wrote about the spate of cybersecurity incidents that led the industry to label last month “Black October.” Now my phone is blowing up, with everyone from colleagues to high school friends asking, what the hell is going on out there?

Are we under attack by a rogue nation? Are outdated software systems suddenly all throwing in the towel? Is this all just cyber-business as usual, with an unusually on-edge public?

According to recent reports, I’m inclined to believe it’s some combination of all of the above. The FBI issued an urgent warning today that bad actors have been using ARTEX, the open-source AI penetration testing platform, to attempt widespread attacks. A source at a financial services tech giant tells me, “It’s been a miserable month…. Just constant probing and hacking attempts.” Companies—and especially government agencies—with outdated software systems are scrambling to patch these vulnerabilities, and are often unable to do so securely without taking their systems entirely offline.

According to recent reports, “What used to take a skilled operator days or weeks of chaining is now happening in hours,” states Snehal Antani, cofounder and CEO of the cybersecurity firm Horizon3. In other words: With AI, bad actors can pretty easily jiggle every doorknob around the globe to see who’s left their doors unlocked.

Meanwhile, the total lack of clarity from the Trump administration hasn’t exactly been reassuring. Even one administration-aligned VC partner I spoke with this morning called the joint presser between Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin a “clown show.”.

For now, I’d urge you to heed the same advice I gave last time I wrote about this: Make sure those passwords are airtight and that multifactor authentication is activated. And maybe, just maybe, stock up on some light supplies you’d like to have around if 21st-century services stop working the way they’re supposed to.

“Going forward, expect this to become normal rather than exceptional,” Antani tells me. “We should expect persistent disruption of digital services—travel, banking, commerce, etc.—in the coming months as these organizations scramble to quickly improve their cyber resilience.”.
